body:
Source: docs/specs/decision-layer-shadow.md, criterion 4 and decisions 9 and 11. Follow-up to T-01M48JH491ZZ77FH2NDMC6EJ20, which ships @adlc/decision-layer with the offline mock provider only.

PREREQUISITE (human). Someone with a TypeSafe API key makes one live call against TypeSafe's documented decision API and commits the request shape and response, with the key and account identifiers removed, as packages/decision-layer/test/fixtures/jev-live-<date>.json, recording the endpoint, model and capture date. No adapter code is written before this fixture exists; the endpoint the earlier branch assumed (https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/decisions) is a starting point, not a fact.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR. A Jev adapter over native fetch implementing the spec's adapter contract: exactly one answer per declared question; no answer obtained (timeout, 429/529, network failure) is `unknown`; an unusable answer (malformed, out of domain, resolved-model mismatch with a pinned request) is `error`; at most 2 retries on 429/529 and network failure, counted in the record; credentials from TYPESAFE_API_KEY falling back to JEV_API_KEY, endpoint override TYPESAFE_API_URL. Once the fixture exists, `--provider jev` stops being a configuration error.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC4 the adapter's tests replay the committed live fixture; unknown vs error classification as above. verify: `node --test packages/decision-layer/test/jev-adapter.test.mjs`
- The default suite still makes no network call. verify: `node --test packages/decision-layer/test/*.test.mjs`

OUT OF SCOPE: everything else in the spec (shipped by T-01M48JH491ZZ77FH2NDMC6EJ20); enforce mode.
title: decision-layer: Jev adapter, built against a captured live response
